hints: Focus on where the H and Br can add, since the double bond in pent-2-ene is not symmetrical.
Adding H to carbon-2 gives 2-bromopentane while adding H to carbon-3 gives 3-bromopentane, so you have two structural isomers to start with.
Now check each bromoalkane for a chiral centre with four different groups, and remember a chiral product counts as two enantiomers.
walkthrough:
**Draw the starting alkene**

Think of trans-pent-2-ene as $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}_3$. The double bond is between carbon-2 and carbon-3.

The trans shape does not stop HBr adding, it just tells us the starting geometry.

**Find the structural isomers from addition**

HBr adds across the $\text{C}=\text{C}$ bond. H can go to carbon-2 and Br to carbon-3, or H to carbon-3 and Br to carbon-2.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}_3 + \text{HBr} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CHBrCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3 \text{ and } \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHBrCH}_2\text{CH}_3$$
That is 2-bromopentane and 3-bromopentane.

**Test each product for chirality**

Look for a carbon with four different groups. In 2-bromopentane, carbon-2 is bonded to $\text{H}$, $\text{Br}$, $\text{CH}_3$ and $\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$.

That is four different groups, so it is chiral and exists as a pair of optical isomers.

**Count the total distinct products**

In 3-bromopentane, carbon-3 is bonded to $\text{H}$, $\text{Br}$ and two identical $\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ groups.

So it is achiral and has only one form. Total = 2 from 2-bromopentane + 1 from 3-bromopentane = 3 different products.

options.A: 1 would only be correct if you thought Markovnikov addition gives a single product and ignored both the second structural isomer and stereoisomerism. In fact both 2-bromo and 3-bromo pentane form.
options.B: 2 counts the two structural isomers, 2-bromopentane and 3-bromopentane, but misses stereoisomerism. It forgets that 2-bromopentane is chiral and splits into two enantiomers.
options.C: 3 is correct. You get 2-bromopentane which is chiral (2 enantiomers) plus 3-bromopentane which is achiral (1 form). That gives 2 + 1 = 3 distinct products.
options.D: 4 would mean both bromoalkanes are chiral with two enantiomers each. But 3-bromopentane has two identical ethyl groups on carbon-3, so it is not chiral and does not have a pair of enantiomers.
